title: Research: bit endpoint and owned-scratch negative results
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

Adds two source-bound negative-result packages. Neither changes the selected κ of 0.001672660197076918 or claims a universal obstruction.

- **Full-frame outputs:** the direct P111 word passes local scalar and bridged-column checks but fails the actual interstage address frames. The complete 5/9/11-stage bills exceed one at zero saving, even with free junction repairs. A separate E8 rotating-normal experiment exhausts its deficit on literal terminal closure. The package explicitly withdraws its earlier local-only optimistic ceilings and identifies the missing idle mass.
- **Owned-zero scratch:** three clean-input implementations replace borrowed-helper restoration with nonzero disposal, late source forks, or a common-frame source decoder. All reproduce the exact target map; the best still costs 5637/4736 at zero saving under an optimistic reverse-call allowance. Its full idle work is included. This rejects these implementations in the retained schedule, not all source-consuming programs.

## Validation

On CPython 3.12.15, with C++17 and Boost headers, from an isolated checkout of canonical main:

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/full-frame-bit-output-probe
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/owned-zero-native-dag
```

Both registered replays passed, including optimized-Python checks. Evidence includes all 111 exact rational port-boundary checks, 444/888/1110 scalar bridge columns, exact rotating-normal closure, three 222-column scratch experiments, source-code inversion and the complete pinned idle schedule. Controls detect changed sources, omitted bridges, omitted target additions and dirty-helper misuse; omitting idle work produces the retained false-positive control.

These are finite checks and written scoped arguments. Full selected-supplier cold replay, all-size/native admission, hosting, precision transfer and Lean verification were not run or established.
